content.comment_body: Hello, I'm [user_name] from Vigo, and this is my first post. I would like to know if it's possible to connect a [product_name] with the [product_name] display and a GSM modem using the current [article_no] version. Is this achievable with the newer [product_name] version that supports Ethernet? Thank you, [user_name]

Hi [user_name]! Unfortunately, you won't be able to connect the INSYS GSM modem to the newer Ethernet-based [product_name] ([article_no]), as these don't include the previous programming port, only Ethernet. Some GSM modems may have an RJ45 Ethernet port—check the INSYS website at [url]. You can connect the [product_name] display to both the earlier [article_no] and the newer [article_no] versions of [product_name]. Hope this helps!

Thank you for your response. So, it seems I cannot use the GSM modem with the new [product_name]. With the older [article_no] version, is it possible to connect both the [product_name] display and the Insys modem at once—for example, to display an alarm on the [product_name] and simultaneously send it to the office via GSM?
Yes, you can connect both the [product_name] display and the Insys modem at the same time. The display uses a separate interface that differs from the one used for the modem.

I've searched for this answer and, as of now, the new [product_name] does not support a GSM modem like the older [product_name] version. However, perhaps [company_name] will release a compatible update in the future.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing the connectivity of a [product_name] with a display and a GSM modem. Feedback indicates that the newer Ethernet models lack legacy programming ports, restricting direct GSM modem use, while the previous versions enable simultaneous connection of a display and GSM modem using separate interfaces. There is hope that forthcoming [company_name] products will support GSM modem connectivity over Ethernet.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want the ability to connect both displays and GSM modems to a [product_name] for local and remote alarm notifications, and anticipate future Ethernet-based [product_name] versions with improved compatibility for GSM modems.
pain_keywords: lack of GSM modem support on Ethernet versions
